60526-jean-of-greenacres.title: Jean Of Greenacres
60526-jean-of-greenacres.creator: Izola L. Forrester
60526-jean-of-greenacres.description: A book by Izola L. Forrester. “He only wanted to know about an express bundle; whether it was hefty or light, and where it came from and if we expected it,” Jean replied, piling the mail on the dining-room table. “There is no mail from Saskatoon, sister fair.”

arxiv-2103-01414.title: A general approach to sample path generation of infinitely divisible processes via shot noise representation 0 0 footnotetext: Email: raykawai@g.ecc.u-tokyo.ac.jp. Postal address: Graduate School of Arts and Sciences / Mathematics and Informatics Center, The University of Tokyo, Japan. The author wo
arxiv-2103-01414.creator: Reiichiro Kawai
arxiv-2103-01414.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Reiichiro Kawai. We establish a sample path generation scheme in a unified manner for general multivariate infinitely divisible processes based on shot noise representation of their integrators. The approximation is derived from the decomposition of the infinitely divisible process to three independent components based on jump sizes and timings: the large jumps over a compact time interval, small jumps over the entire time interval and large jumps over an unbounded time interval.

arxiv-2104-08564.title: A Novel Non-population-based Meta-heuristic Optimizer Inspired by the Philosophy of Yi Jing
arxiv-2104-08564.creator: Ho-Kin Tang, Sim Kuan Goh
arxiv-2104-08564.description: Abstract Drawing inspiration from the philosophy of Yi Jing, Yin-Yang pair optimization (YYPO) has been shown to achieve competitive performance in single objective optimizations. Besides, it has the advantage of low time complexity when comparing to other population-based optimization. As a conceptual extension of YYPO, we proposed the novel Yi optimization (YI) algorithm as one of the best non-population-based optimizer.

arxiv-2105-13002.title: Risk Quantization by Magnitude and Propensity
arxiv-2105-13002.creator: Olivier P. Faugeras, Gilles Pagès
arxiv-2105-13002.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Olivier P. Faugeras, Gilles Pagès. We propose a novel approach in the assessment of a random risk variable X X by introducing magnitude-propensity risk measures ( m X , p X ) (m_{X},p_{X}) . This bivariate measure intends to account for the dual aspect of risk, where the magnitudes x x of X X tell how hign are the losses incurred, whereas the probabilities P ⁡ ( X = x ) P(X=x) reveal how often one has to expect to suffer such losses.

arxiv-2107-01780.title: The refined local lifting problem for cyclic covers of order four The author is supported by the Vietnam Institute for Advanced Study in Mathematics and the Simons Foundation Grant Targeted for Institute of Mathematics, Vietnam Academy of Science and Technology.
arxiv-2107-01780.creator: Huy Dang
arxiv-2107-01780.description: Abstract Suppose ϕ \phi is a ℤ / 4 \mathbb{Z}/4 -cover of a curve over an algebraically closed field k k of characteristic 2 2 , and Φ 1 \Phi_{1} is a nice lift of ϕ \phi ’s ℤ / 2 \mathbb{Z}/2 -sub-cover to a complete discrete valuation ring R R in characteristic zero.

arxiv-2303-15611.title: Converging Periodic Boundary Conditions and Detection of Topological Gaps on Regular Hyperbolic Tessellations
arxiv-2303-15611.creator: Fabian R. Lux, Emil Prodan
arxiv-2303-15611.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Fabian R. Lux, Emil Prodan. Tessellations of the hyperbolic spaces by regular polygons are becoming popular because they support discrete quantum and classical models displaying unique spectral and topological characteristics. Resolving the true bulk spectra and the thermodynamic response functions of these models requires converging periodic boundary conditions and our work delivers a practical solution for this open problem on generic { p , q } \{p,q\} -tessellations.

arxiv-2308-14736.title: The Artin-Hasse series and Laguerre polynomials modulo a prime
arxiv-2308-14736.creator: Marina Avitabile, Sandro Mattarei
arxiv-2308-14736.description: Abstract . For an odd prime p p , let E p ⁡ ( X ) = ∑ n = 0 ∞ a n ​ X n ∈ 𝔽 p ​ [ [ X ] ] \E_{p}(X)=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}a_{n}X^{n}\in\mathbb{F}_{p}[[X]] denote the reduction modulo p p of the Artin-Hasse exponential series.

arxiv-2310-01571.title: Contraction Properties of the Global Workspace Primitive
arxiv-2310-01571.creator: Michaela Ennis, Leo Kozachkov, Jean-Jacques Slotine
arxiv-2310-01571.description: Abstract To push forward the important emerging research field surrounding multi-area recurrent neural networks (RNNs), we expand theoretically and empirically on the provably stable "RNNs of RNNs" introduced by Kozachkov et al. 2022 . We prove relaxed stability conditions for salient special cases of this architecture, most notably for a global workspace modular structure.

arxiv-2504-21323.title: How to Backdoor the Knowledge Distillation
arxiv-2504-21323.creator: Chen Wu, Qian Ma, Prasenjit Mitra, Sencun Zhu
arxiv-2504-21323.description: Abstract Knowledge distillation has become a cornerstone in modern machine learning systems, celebrated for its ability to transfer knowledge from a large, complex teacher model to a more efficient student model. Traditionally, this process is regarded as secure, assuming the teacher model is clean.

arxiv-2505-07357.title: Analytical gradients of random-phase approximation plus corrections from renormalized single excitations
arxiv-2505-07357.creator: Muhammad N. Tahir, Honghui Shang, Xinguo Ren
arxiv-2505-07357.description: Abstract The random-phase approximation (RPA) formulated within the adiabatic connection fluctuation-dissipation framework is a powerful approach to compute the ground-state energies and properties of molecules and materials. Its overall underbinding behavior can be effectively mitigated by a simple correction term, called renormalized single excitation (rSE) correction.

arxiv-2505-18410.title: On Theoretical Identifiability of Discrete Latent Causal Graphical Models
arxiv-2505-18410.creator: Seunghyun Lee sl4963@columbia.edu, Yuqi Gu yuqi.gu@columbia.edu
arxiv-2505-18410.description: Abstract This paper considers a challenging problem of identifying a causal graphical model under the presence of latent variables. While various identifiability conditions have been proposed in the literature, they often require multiple pure children per latent variable or restrictions on the latent causal graph. Furthermore, it is common for all observed variables to exhibit the same modality.

arxiv-2506-09895.title: EquiCaps: Predictor-Free Pose-Aware Pre-Trained Capsule Networks
arxiv-2506-09895.creator: Athinoulla Konstantinou, Georgios Leontidis, Mamatha Thota, Aiden Durrant, Interdisciplinary Institute University of Aberdeen, UK
arxiv-2506-09895.description: Abstract Learning self-supervised representations that are invariant and equivariant to transformations is crucial for advancing beyond traditional visual classification tasks. However, many methods rely on predictor architectures to encode equivariance, despite evidence that architectural choices, such as capsule networks, inherently excel at learning interpretable pose-aware representations.

arxiv-2507-08066.title: Kappa Plane Wave Modes and Continuous Squeezing in Quantum Field Theory
arxiv-2507-08066.creator: Arash Azizi
arxiv-2507-08066.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Arash Azizi. We introduce a new family of field modes in flat spacetime—termed κ \kappa -plane wave modes —constructed from κ \kappa -dependent linear combinations of Minkowski plane waves. These modes define a one-parameter family of vacua | 0 κ ⟩ \ket{0_\kappa} that smoothly interpolate between different quantizations, reducing to the Minkowski vacuum in the limit κ → 0 \kappa\to 0 .

arxiv-2509-04275.title: Polynomial stability of non-linearly damped contraction semigroups Thanks: This work was supported by the Research Council of Finland Grant number 349002 and by the Heilbronn Institute for Mathematical Research.
arxiv-2509-04275.creator: Lassi Paunonen, David Seifert
arxiv-2509-04275.description: Abstract . We investigate the stability properties of an abstract class of semi-linear systems. Our main result establishes rational rates of decay for classical solutions assuming a certain non-uniform observability estimate for the linear part and suitable conditions on the non-linearity.

arxiv-2601-05514.title: Emergence of the 2nd Law in an Exactly Solvable Model of a Quantum Wire
arxiv-2601-05514.creator: Marco A. Jimenez-Valencia, Charles A. Stafford
arxiv-2601-05514.description: Abstract As remarked by Boltzmann, the Second Law of Thermodynamics is notable for the fact that it is readily proved using elementary statistical arguments, but becomes harder and harder to verify the more precise the microscopic description of a system.

arxiv-2601-11775.title: Quantum Kernel Machine Learning for Autonomous Materials Science
arxiv-2601-11775.creator: Felix Adams, Daiwei Zhu, David W. Steuerman, A. Gilad Kusne, Ichiro Takeuchi
arxiv-2601-11775.description: Abstract Autonomous materials science, where active learning is used to navigate large compositional phase space, has emerged as a powerful vehicle to rapidly explore new materials. A crucial aspect of autonomous materials science is exploring new materials using as little data as possible.

britannica-1911-temper.title: Temper (1911 Encyclopaedia Britannica article)
britannica-1911-temper.creator: Encyclopaedia Britannica
britannica-1911-temper.description: Article 'Temper' from the 1911 Encyclopædia Britannica (Volume 26), the classic English-language general encyclopedia, now in the public domain. formed from tempus, time, fit or due season), to blend, modify, or qualify by mixing, to combine in due proportions, hence to restrain, calm. A specific application of the word is to the bringing of steel or other metal to a proper hardness and elasticity (see Metal and Iron and Steel).

europmc-pmc4818766.title: Mitochondria are required for pro-ageing features of the senescent phenotype.
europmc-pmc4818766.creator: Correia-Melo C, Marques FD, Anderson R, Hewitt G, Hewitt R, Cole J, Carroll BM, Miwa S, Birch J, Merz A, Rushton MD, Charles M, Jurk D, Tait SW, Czapiewski R, Greaves L, Nelson G, Bohlooly-Y M, Rodriguez-Cuenca S, Vidal-Puig A, Mann D, Saretzki G, Quarato G, Green DR, Adams PD, von Zglinicki T, Korolchuk VI, Passos JF.
europmc-pmc4818766.description: Cell senescence is an important tumour suppressor mechanism and driver of ageing. Both functions are dependent on the development of the senescent phenotype, which involves an overproduction of pro-inflammatory and pro-oxidant signals. However, the exact mechanisms regulating...

govdocs-nsarchive-Briefing_Book_china_Re.creator: National Security Archive
govdocs-nsarchive-Briefing_Book_china_Re.description: National Security Archive Electronic Briefing Book publishing declassified records. Washington, D.C., October 16, 2020 - Over the years, aerial and naval encounters have threatened to destabilize U.S-China relations as the two powers contest each other's rights in international airspace and waters. Edited by William Burr.

pmc-11506334.title: Acute Levodopa Challenge in Atypical Parkinsonism: Comprehensive Analysis of Individual Motor Responses
pmc-11506334.creator: Lan Ye, Sam Sadeghi Sani, Linda Veith Sanches, Lea Farina Magdalena Krey, Florian Wegner, Matthias Höllerhage, Christoph Schrader, Günter Höglinger, Martin Klietz, Abdelaziz M Hussein
pmc-11506334.description: The acute levodopa challenge is widely used to distinguish Parkinson’s disease (PD) from atypical parkinsonian syndromes (APSs) such as multiple system atrophy (MSA) and progressive supranuclear palsy (PSP). In APSs, very few patients present a clinically relevant response to levodopa.

pmc-11511316.title: Experimental Investigations of Assessment of Acute Toxicity of Drilling Mud
pmc-11511316.creator: Arstan Mamyrbayev, Saule Bermagambetova, Kuanysh Baytenov, Zhanat Komekbay, Laura Sakebayeva, Umit Satybaldiyeva, Gulmira Yerimbetova, Kulyash Zhilisbayeva, Tapani Tuomi
pmc-11511316.description: At present, the main technological stages of oil production related to drilling operations require the use of a wide variety of drilling mud, which has a complex, multicomponent chemical composition. The drilling mud used and the resulting drilling waste must be safe for human health and the environment.

pmc-11531615.title: ARID1A loss sensitizes colorectal cancer cells to floxuridine
pmc-11531615.creator: Cheng Xiang, Zhen Wang, Yingnan Yu, Zelong Han, Jingyi Lu, Lei Pan, Xu Zhang, Zihuan Wang, Yilin He, Kejin Wang, Wenxuan Peng, Side Liu, Yijiang Song, Changjie Wu
pmc-11531615.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). The loss-of-function mutation of AT-rich interactive domain 1A (ARID1A) frequently occurs in various types of cancer, making it a promising therapeutic target. In the present study, we performed a screening of an FDA-approved drug library in ARID1A isogenic colorectal cancer (CRC) cells and discovered that ARID1A loss sensitizes CRC cells to floxuridine (FUDR), an antineoplastic agent used for treating hepatic metastases from CRC, both in vivo and in vitro.

pmc-11568460.title: A Nature-Based Intervention and Mental Health of Schoolchildren
pmc-11568460.creator: Tianna Loose, Julia Fuoco, Catherine Malboeuf-Hurtubise, Jean-Philippe Ayotte-Beaudet, Lise Gauvin, Nicholas Chadi, Isabelle Ouellet-Morin, Benoît Mâsse, Sylvana M. Côté, Marie-Claude Geoffroy
pmc-11568460.description: This cluster randomized clinical trial investigates the effectiveness of a nature-based outdoor educational intervention for reducing mental health symptoms among elementary school students in grades 5 and 6. Introduction Observational studies suggest that time outdoors (ie, in nature) benefits the mental health of adults and children.

pmc-11659249.title: Cognitive dysfunction in Moyamoya disease: latest developments and future directions
pmc-11659249.creator: Xilong Wang, Ziqi Liu, Zhenyu Zhou, Junze Zhang, Yanru Wang, Shihao He, Rong Wang
pmc-11659249.description: Cognitive dysfunction is common in Moyamoya disease (MMD). However, current knowledge of cognitive impairment in MMD is inadequate. In this review, we explored the characteristics of altered cognitive function associated with MMD and offered recommendations aimed at guiding potential research endeavors into the cognitive dysfunction in MMD.

pmc-12650494.title: Low-Overhead Learning: Quantized Shallow Neural Networks at the Service of Genetic Algorithm Optimization
pmc-12650494.creator: Fabián Pizarro, Emanuel Vega, Ricardo Soto, Broderick Crawford, José Villamayor
pmc-12650494.description: Online parameter tuning significantly enhances the performance of optimization algorithms by dynamically adjusting mutation and crossover rates. However, current approaches often suffer from high computational costs and limited adaptability to complex and dynamic fitness landscapes, particularly when machine learning methods are employed.

pmc-12784953.title: Age and Clinical Outcomes of Immune Checkpoint Inhibitor Toxicities in Portugal: A Decade of Pharmacovigilance
pmc-12784953.creator: Tiago Pina-Cabral, José Pereira, João Paulo-Fernandes, Márcia Silva, Mário Fontes-Sousa, Mariana Anacleto, Soraia Lobo-Martins, Ana Mirco, Helena Miranda, Ana Martins, Patrícia Cavaco
pmc-12784953.description: Simple SummaryImmune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) are widely used across many cancer types, yet their real-world safety in older adults is not well studied. Using a decade of national pharmacovigilance data from Portugal, we examined adverse drug reactions (ADRs) reported in patients treated with ICIs, focusing on whether age impacts the seriousness or pattern of toxicities.

pmc-12915351.title: Ambient Air Pollution and Cardiometabolic Health in the Tehran Lipid and Glucose Study: A Scoping Review of Two Decades of Evidence
pmc-12915351.creator: Amir Hossein Hasanpour, Mohammad Javad Mansourzadeh, Alireza Khajavi, Fereidoun Azizi, Farzad Hadaegh
pmc-12915351.description: ContextThis scoping review investigates the association between ambient air pollution and cardiometabolic outcomes using data from the Tehran Lipid and Glucose Study (TLGS), a population-based cohort initiated in 1999.Evidence AcquisitionFive TLGS studies were included, each examining associations between ambient air pollutants and cardiometabolic outcomes such as hypertension (HTN), dyslipidemia, diabetes, cardiovascular morbidity, and mortality.

pmc-13652761.title: Outpatient drug therapy for children with heart disease in Switzerland: a survey
pmc-13652761.creator: Joel Bärlocher, Angela Caduff Good, Stefano Di Bernardo, Sebastiano A G Lava, Dominik Stambach, Cécile Tissot, Walter Knirsch, Julie Wacker, Anna Cavigelli-Brunner, Alessandra Bosch, Christian Balmer
pmc-13652761.description: Cardiovascular drug therapy in adults is steadily progressing. However, the extent to which children with heart disease in Switzerland benefit from this progress remains unknown. This survey aimed to investigate the current outpatient prescribing practices among paediatric cardiologists in Switzerland. We conducted a cross-sectional survey among Swiss paediatric cardiologists.
